instruction: In the calendar spreadsheet, highlight all June weekend dates (Saturdays and Sundays in column B) by setting their cell background to red (#ff0000).

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to highlight all weekend dates across 5 months but failed. It correctly identified June 4-5 as Saturday-Sunday and selected B6:B7, applied partial red background. Then tried using Name Box with comma-separated multi-range but got a syntax error. Only managed to partially color a few cells in June and July columns, with incorrect row mappings for other months.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open LibreOffice Calc, navigate cells, select cell ranges, apply background colors via highlighting button, use Name Box for cell selection
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed because: (1) incorrectly mapped date-to-row for months other than June, (2) used commas instead of semicolons for Name Box multi-range selection, (3) ran out of turns after error recovery attempts. Only ~2 of 44 total weekend cells were highlighted.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified original 5-month weekend highlighting to just June (column B) - 8 cells in a single column. This matches the model's demonstrated ability to identify June weekends and apply colors.
metadata.explanation: Task requires setting red background on 8 cells in column B that correspond to June 2022 weekends (Sat: B6,B13,B20,B27; Sun: B7,B14,B21,B28). Getter reads fill colors of these cells. Metric checks each cell has FF0000 color with partial credit.

scoring_breakdown.each_cell: 0.125 per correctly colored cell (8 cells total)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads cell background colors using openpyxl, handling both fgColor.rgb and start_color.rgb for solid fills
Metric correctly accesses expected parameter as rules dict directly (expected.get('expected_color'), expected.get('cells')) - proper handling for type='rule'
Cell references B6,B7,B13,B14,B20,B21,B27,B28 are consistent with a weekly calendar layout (7-row spacing) for June 2022 weekends (4 Saturdays + 4 Sundays = 8 cells)
Substring color check 'FF0000 in actual.upper()' correctly handles ARGB format (e.g., FFFF0000 from openpyxl)
Partial credit scoring (correct/total) is appropriate for multi-cell verification
Postconfig saves file via Ctrl+S before getter reads it, ensuring fresh state
Complete coverage: all 8 June weekend cells are checked for the required red background color
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Consider using exact color match (e.g., actual.upper() in ['FF0000', 'FFFF0000']) instead of substring 'in' check to avoid theoretical false positives with colors containing 'FF0000' as substring
